fullTitle: Prevalence of Malaria–Dengue Coinfection Among Febrile Patients, Port Sudan Teaching Hospital
description: Febrile patients at Port Sudan Teaching Hospital were tested to determine malaria–dengue coinfection prevalence. Coinfection was the most common diagnosis (40.1%), associated with longer hospital stays and higher complication rates than either infection alone.
researchQuestion: What is the prevalence and clinical impact of malaria–dengue coinfection among febrile patients in a dual-endemic setting?

shortTitle: Diarrhoeal Disease in Displaced Children — Atbara
fullTitle: Diarrhoeal Disease Among Displaced Children in Atbara City
description: Displaced children aged 7–12 in Atbara's Alnhda Camp were surveyed to identify determinants of diarrhoeal disease. Prevalence reached 70.7%, with access to tap water the strongest protective factor against illness.
researchQuestion: What WASH, behavioural, and sociodemographic factors predict diarrhoeal disease among displaced children aged 7–12?

fullTitle: Evaluation of a Diarrheal Prevention Program Among Internally Displaced Persons — Marwi Camps
description: A structured health education intervention was evaluated among IDP community members in Marwi Camps using pre/post KAP surveys. All KAP measures improved significantly, and household diarrhoea prevalence fell from 42.2% to 33.6%.
researchQuestion: Does a structured diarrhoeal prevention education programme improve KAP and reduce diarrhoea prevalence among displaced communities?

shortTitle: Cholera Risk Factors — OIU Medical Students
fullTitle: Knowledge, Awareness and Attitudes of Clinical Medical Students Toward Cholera
description: Clinical-year medical students at Omdurman Islamic University were surveyed to assess cholera knowledge, attitudes, and preventive compliance. Formal lectures were the strongest predictor of good compliance, while fifth-years showed a 'compliance fatigue' pattern.
researchQuestion: How prepared are clinical-year medical students to detect, manage, and prevent cholera, and what predicts good compliance?

fullTitle: Vaccination Status Among Children in Port Sudan Displacement Camps During Armed Conflict
description: Caregivers in Port Sudan displacement camps were surveyed on childhood vaccination coverage and access barriers. Full coverage reached 66.8%, with vaccination card possession and trust in services the strongest predictors of complete vaccination.
researchQuestion: What structural and informational barriers determine full childhood vaccination status in displacement camps?

fullTitle: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Compliance with TB Preventive Measures Among Clinical-Year Students at Omdurman Islamic University
description: Clinical-year students across Medicine, Nursing, and Laboratory Sciences were surveyed on TB knowledge, attitudes, and compliance. Counterintuitively, knowledge was inversely associated with compliance, informing how future TB education should be designed.
researchQuestion: Does TB knowledge translate into compliance with preventive measures among clinical-year students, and what explains the gap?

shortTitle: Infection Control at Referral Centres — Jabel Awlia
fullTitle: Infection Control Measures at Referral Health Care Centers — Jabel Awlia Locality
description: All 11 functioning referral health centres in Jabel Awlia Locality were assessed against WHO infection prevention and control structural requirements. Overall compliance was just 22.6%, with complete non-compliance in healthcare-worker safety and device reprocessing.
researchQuestion: Do referral health centres meet the structural requirements for a functional infection prevention and control programme?

fullTitle: Medical Students' Adherence to Infection Prevention Practices — Omdurman Islamic University
description: Clinical-year medical students were surveyed on infection prevention knowledge and adherence. Senior staff compliance was the strongest independent predictor of student adherence, more so than knowledge or formal training.
researchQuestion: What predicts good infection prevention adherence among clinical-year medical students — knowledge, training, or environment?

shortTitle: Conflict Zones & Dengue Fever — OIU Students
fullTitle: The Impact of Conflict Zones on Medical Students at Omdurman Islamic University: A Case Study of Dengue Fever
description: Medical students at Omdurman Islamic University were surveyed on conflict exposure, dengue fever diagnosis, and psychological/academic impact. 60% had been diagnosed with dengue, and conflict impact and healthcare access barriers independently predicted psychological symptoms.
researchQuestion: How do armed conflict exposure and a concurrent dengue outbreak jointly affect medical students' academic, clinical, and psychological outcomes?

fullTitle: Depression Among Type 1 Diabetes Patients — Atbra Teaching Hospital
description: Type 1 diabetes patients at Atbra Teaching Hospital were assessed for depression using the Hamilton Depression Rating Scale. Prevalence reached 75%, with foot ulcers and poor glycemic monitoring the strongest independent predictors.
researchQuestion: What is the prevalence of depression among Type 1 diabetes patients, and which clinical factors predict it?

shortTitle: Depression Among Sudanese Doctors — Saudi Arabia
fullTitle: Depression Among Sudanese Doctors in Saudi Arabia During the War Period
description: Sudanese physicians displaced to Saudi Arabia were surveyed using the PHQ-9 to estimate depression prevalence. 40.1% met criteria for clinically significant depression, with financial hardship the strongest predictor and suicidal ideation reported by 29.3%.
researchQuestion: What is the prevalence of depression among Sudanese doctors displaced by the war, and what drives it?

shortTitle: Clinical Rotation Stress & Immune Health — OIU
fullTitle: Impact of Clinical Rotation Stress on Psychological Wellbeing and Immune Health — OIU
description: Clinical-year medical students were assessed for rotation-related stress, psychological distress, and perceived immune health. Over 60% showed clinically significant depression and anxiety, with immune complaints linked to distress severity.
researchQuestion: How does clinical rotation stress relate to psychological wellbeing and perceived immune health in medical students?

fullTitle: NCD Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Among Medical Students — University of Gezira
description: Undergraduate medical students at the University of Gezira were surveyed on non-communicable disease knowledge, attitudes, and prevention practices. Despite near-universal knowledge, only 14% regularly checked their own blood pressure — a stark knowledge-practice gap.
researchQuestion: Does high NCD knowledge among medical students translate into personal preventive behaviour?

fullTitle: Effect of Irritable Bowel Syndrome on Academic Performance of Medical Students, Omdurman Islamic University
description: Medical students were screened for IBS using Rome IV criteria and assessed across six academic performance domains. IBS prevalence was 30.4%, significantly higher in females, and associated with a medium-to-large drop in composite academic performance.
researchQuestion: Does IBS diagnosis measurably impair academic performance among medical students?

fullTitle: ChatGPT Use and Academic Performance Among Medical Students
description: Medical students at Omdurman Islamic University were surveyed on ChatGPT use and its relationship to perceived academic benefit. 80% were frequent users, and usage frequency correlated positively with perceived benefit — though students who received institutional AI training reported lower perception scores.
researchQuestion: How does ChatGPT use relate to medical students' learning behaviour and perceived academic benefit?

shortTitle: Tuition Fees and Academic Performance — OIU
fullTitle: The Impact of High Tuition Fees on Academic Performance of Medical Students at Omdurman Islamic University
description: Medical students were surveyed on financial stress from tuition fees and its relationship to GPA. Financial stress correlated significantly with lower GPA, though the fee amount itself did not — the student's financial capacity mattered more than the fee level.
researchQuestion: Does tuition-related financial stress predict academic performance among medical students?

fullTitle: Motivations for Choosing Medicine and Psychological and Social Effects — OIU
description: Medical students were surveyed on their motivations for entering medicine and resulting psychological and social effects. Intrinsic motivation showed no adverse effects, while extrinsic and family-driven motivation independently predicted higher psychological distress.
researchQuestion: Does the type of motivation for choosing medicine (intrinsic vs. extrinsic) predict psychological distress?

shortTitle: Sudan War Impact on Life Priorities — OIU
fullTitle: Impact of the Sudan War (2023–2025) on the Life Priorities of Medical Students at Omdurman Islamic University
description: Medical students displaced by the Sudan war were surveyed on war exposure, distress, and life priority rankings. Contrary to expectations, academic goals ranked narrowly above survival, challenging assumptions about priority hierarchies under conflict.
researchQuestion: How does armed conflict reorganise the relative priority of survival, migration, and academic pursuit among medical students?

fullTitle: Barriers and Factors Influencing Postgraduate Career Decisions Among Ophthalmology Residents and Ophthalmologists in Sudan
description: Ophthalmology residents and ophthalmologists across Sudan were surveyed on factors shaping postgraduate career decisions. Personal interest and work-life balance ranked highest, while macro-level instability — economic crisis and political conflict — dominated the barriers list.
researchQuestion: What factors most strongly influence postgraduate career decisions among ophthalmology trainees during conflict?

fullTitle: Family Planning Among Married Women of Reproductive Age in Kassala City
sampleSize: N = 384 married women of reproductive age
description: Married women of reproductive age in Kassala City were surveyed on family planning use and its social determinants. Husband's attitude was the dominant predictor — 96.5% of women with supportive husbands were current users, compared to 0% when husbands were unaware of use.
researchQuestion: What social and structural factors drive family planning uptake among married women in Kassala?

fullTitle: Assessment of Community Awareness Toward Well-Baby Clinic Services, Al-Sana'at Administrative Unit
description: Caregivers of children under five in a rural Gezira community were surveyed on well-baby clinic knowledge, attitudes, and use. Knowledge was low (60% poor) despite strongly positive attitudes, indicating the barrier is informational rather than attitudinal.
researchQuestion: What accounts for low well-baby clinic utilisation in a rural community — knowledge, attitude, or access barriers?

fullTitle: Patient Satisfaction in Primary Healthcare Settings During the War in Sudan — Eleskan75 Center
description: Patients at a high-burden primary healthcare centre in Omdurman were surveyed on satisfaction during the ongoing conflict. 75.6% were satisfied overall, with women reporting significantly higher satisfaction than men across most domains.
researchQuestion: How satisfied are patients with primary healthcare services delivered under active conflict conditions?

fullTitle: Knowledge, Attitudes, and Practices Toward Telemedicine Among Primary Healthcare Physicians in Sudan
description: Primary healthcare physicians across Sudan were surveyed on telemedicine knowledge, attitudes, and use. Physicians who received formal training were far more positive (75.6% vs. 25.7%), suggesting training — not infrastructure alone — is the key lever for adoption.
researchQuestion: What factors shape primary healthcare physicians' adoption of and attitude toward telemedicine in Sudan?
